description:
## Why

`pkix-profiles-cabf`'s `SmimeProfile` currently implements the Mailbox-validated / strict tier only. CA/B Forum S/MIME Baseline Requirements define **four** mailbox-binding tiers:

1. **Mailbox-validated** — proven control of the mailbox. (Done — current `SmimeProfile` in `pkix-profiles-cabf`.)
2. **Organization-validated** — mailbox + verified ownership of the organization domain. Distinct issuance vetting rules.
3. **Sponsor-validated** — sponsor (often an employer) vouches for the individual. Includes `sponsor` field semantics.
4. **Individual-validated** — individual identity proofed (passport, driver's license, etc.). Strictest non-organization tier.

Each tier has its own required Subject DN fields, allowed SANs, and policy OID. A single `SmimeProfile` cannot represent all four because the validation predicates differ.

## Where this work lives

`pkix-profiles-cabf` — **not** `pkix-profiles`. Under the framework-not-policy stance (PKIX-amgn, AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6) the main `pkix-profiles` crate ships RFC-baseline policy only (`BasicSmimeProfile` per RFC 8551 §3). CA/B Forum-specific content lives in `pkix-profiles-cabf` and is marked "reference / not authoritative" — CA/B Forum publishes only PDFs, so any machine-readable encoding is an interpretation, not the authority.

## What

Three new profile types alongside the existing `SmimeProfile` in `pkix-profiles-cabf` (or four total if Mailbox-validated is renamed for clarity to mirror the BR-tier naming):

```rust
pub struct SmimeMailboxValidated;          // current SmimeProfile, possibly renamed
pub struct SmimeOrganizationValidated;
pub struct SmimeSponsorValidated;
pub struct SmimeIndividualValidated;
```

Each impls `Profile` (the trait still lives in `pkix-profiles`; `pkix-profiles-cabf` consumes it) with its own `policy(now_unix)` returning the appropriate `ValidationPolicy`. Per CA/B Forum S/MIME BR v1.0:

- Different required Subject DN fields (givenName + surname for Individual; orgName + orgUnit for Organization; etc.).
- Different required SAN content (rfc822Name for all; X.500 distinguishedName when present must match Subject for stricter tiers).
- Different policy OID assertion required on the cert.
- Same `max_validity_secs` cap (SC-081, applies to all tiers).

Each new type may extend or compose atop `pkix_profiles::BasicSmimeProfile` (the RFC 8551 §3 baseline) rather than duplicating its checks.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Three new profile types compile + impl `Profile` in `pkix-profiles-cabf`.
- [ ] Each has a corresponding free-function alias (`smime_org_policy`, `smime_sponsor_policy`, `smime_individual_policy`).
- [ ] **Each new profile type carries the same "reference, not authoritative" rustdoc disclaimer header that `pkix-profiles-cabf`'s existing types carry**, pointing readers at the live CA/B Forum S/MIME BR text for the binding source.
- [ ] Each new profile type's rustdoc cites the CA/B Forum S/MIME BR version it was interpreted against, so future BR revisions can be tracked.
- [ ] Test cert per tier validates against the right profile, fails against the wrong one. Test certs are independently sourced or generated; do NOT rely on `pkix-profiles-cabf`'s own profile types to produce the expected verdict (AGENTS.md test-integrity rule).
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry in `pkix-profiles-cabf` (not `pkix-profiles`).
- [ ] No content moves into `pkix-profiles`; the main crate stays framework + RFC-baseline only.

## Decomposition (file children when work starts)

1. Organization-validated profile + tests.
2. Sponsor-validated profile + tests.
3. Individual-validated profile + tests.

## Depends on

- **PKIX-amgn.2** (`pkix-profiles-cabf` workspace crate exists) — CLOSED 2026-05-11.
- **PKIX-amgn.4** (`BasicSmimeProfile` in `pkix-profiles` exists for compose-atop) — CLOSED 2026-05-11.

Both dependencies are CLOSED at the time of this retargeting; the bead is unblocked for autonomous claim.

## Filed as

Tracker for the original `pkix-profiles/src/lib.rs` "planned" rustdoc references, surfaced by the PKIX-agp7.2 sweep audit. Retargeted to `pkix-profiles-cabf` by PKIX-amgn.6 (2026-05-11) under the framework-not-policy stance.

Decisions recorded 2026-05-11 (Mark):

(1) CA/B Forum S/MIME BR version pin: follow whichever revision zlint pins. This defers the version-tracking burden to PKIX-amgn.8 (vendor zlint catalog as OSCAL Catalog JSON). When zlint bumps to a new BR revision, our reference interpretation tracks via the next catalog vendor refresh. Adds a real blocks edge from PKIX-amgn.8 -> PKIX-jbvb so this bead does not surface as ready until the zlint catalog is in place to anchor the version.

(2) Test cert sourcing: option (d) — pull from BOTH zlint testdata/ AND pkilint fixtures. Cross-validation between the two dominant ecosystem interpretations earns the "useful even if not authoritative" framing. Where zlint and pkilint diverge on a fixture, our profile validation result is informational; where they agree, agreement with both is the bar for pkix-profiles-cabf correctness on that fixture. Both upstreams are Apache-2.0 and citable; record provenance per-fixture in CHANGELOG.

human label removed; bead is now blocked-on-deps cascade.
[2026-05-13 do-beads loop escalation]

do-beads loop autonomously-eligible work surfaced a substantive gap: PKIX-jbvb.1/.2/.3 cannot land as currently described because ValidationPolicy doesn't support the predicates each S/MIME sub-profile needs to actually distinguish itself from the existing SmimeProfile.

THE GAP:
The CA/B Forum S/MIME BR distinguishes the four mailbox-validated tiers (Mailbox-/Organization-/Sponsor-/Individual-validated) via:
- Required Subject DN attributes (e.g., organizationName for Org-validated; givenName+surname for Individual)
- Asserted certificate policy OID (2.23.140.1.5.1.x family; one per tier)
- Per-tier SAN content rules

pkix_path::ValidationPolicy currently exposes (audit of pkix-path/src/lib.rs:614-744):
- max_path_len, current_time_unix, enforce_key_usage, require_crl_sign_on_cas
- initial_explicit_policy, initial_any_policy_inhibit, initial_policy_mapping_inhibit, initial_policy_set
- max_validity_secs, allowed_signature_algs, min_rsa_key_bits
- require_subject_alt_name, require_rfc822_san, required_leaf_eku

It does NOT have:
- required_policy_oids (initial_policy_set is the RP's acceptable set, not "this OID MUST be asserted on the leaf")
- required_subject_dn_attributes

Without these, the four S/MIME sub-profiles' policy() outputs would be byte-identical to each other and to the current SmimeProfile. The only difference would be id(), version(), and the advisory policy_oids() slice — none of which path-validation actually checks. The marquee-reference value of distinct types collapses.

OPTIONS:

(A) Extend pkix_path::ValidationPolicy with new fields (required_policy_oids, required_subject_dn_attributes) and wire enforcement into chain_walk. Largest scope. Affects pkix-path's 1.0 API freeze (PKIX-wlsr.3 ratified the current shape) — would need explicit re-decision. Each new field is also a maintenance commitment the workspace takes on for every consumer's profile.

(B) Ship Profile shells whose policy() output IS identical across tiers, but pair them with -chain wrapper variants (verify_smime_signer_organization, etc.) that do per-tier post-validation checks against the chain leaf — Subject DN attribute presence + asserted policy OID. The Profile type then carries "tier identity" as a type-system invariant, even though path-validation alone can't distinguish them. Closer to how verify_time_stamper post-checks RFC 3161 §2.3.

(C) Ship Profile shells with only the predicates ValidationPolicy already supports. Acknowledge in rustdoc that "tier disambiguation requires additional caller-side checks; for predicate-comprehensive enforcement use pkix-policy-zlint." Smallest surface, weakest marquee-reference value.

(D) Defer until pkix-policy-zlint demonstrates that zlint's CA/B Forum S/MIME catalog already covers the predicates. If yes, drop PKIX-jbvb.1/.2/.3 as redundant with the principled-path predicate-comprehensive coverage.

RECOMMENDATION: (B). It preserves the spec-taxonomy principle's intent (one Profile per BR-named subscriber-cert tier) and uses the same composition pattern as the existing -chain TLS/S/MIME/CodeSign/Timestamp wrappers, which the workspace already endorsed. (A) is over-reach for pre-1.0 (the new fields would only be used by S/MIME sub-profiles, which is one consumer); (C) doesn't justify shipping four near-identical types; (D) gives up the principle.

SECONDARY GAP — test fixtures: PKIX-jbvb.1's acceptance spec requires fixtures from ~/GIT/zlint/v3/lints/cabf_smime/*/testdata/ and ~/GIT/pkilint/tests/integration_certificates/cabf/smime/. Neither directory exists. AGENTS.md allows shallow-cloning into ~/GIT but the bead also conflates predicate enforcement (the substantive question above) with fixture sourcing. Resolving the substantive question first makes the fixture question concrete; pre-emptive cloning would be premature.

Skipping all three (.1/.2/.3) per the loop's "one decision, many beads" principle; the question is the same for each tier and Mark can answer once.
[2026-05-13 design decision LOCKED by Mark]

Option A with a small expression type for Subject DN attribute rules. Chosen over option B because the load-bearing objection ("affects pkix-path's 1.0 API freeze") was wrong — ValidationPolicy is already #[non_exhaustive] + Default, and the existing required_leaf_eku: Option<Vec<Oid>> field is direct precedent for additive leaf-only predicate fields.

DESIGN:
- pkix-path::ValidationPolicy gains TWO new fields:
  * required_leaf_policy_oids: Option<Vec<ObjectIdentifier>> — flat list. Leaf cert's CertificatePolicies extension must assert every OID in this list.
  * required_leaf_subject_dn_attrs: Option<DnAttrRule> — expression type for compositional rules (supports the BR's 'pseudonym OR (givenName + surname)' pattern for Individual / Sponsor tiers).
- New enum:
    pub enum DnAttrRule {
        Field(ObjectIdentifier),
        AllOf(Vec<DnAttrRule>),
        AnyOf(Vec<DnAttrRule>),
    }
- Enforcement in chain_walk (leaf-only), same code site as required_leaf_eku.
- New Error variants on pkix-path::Error (non_exhaustive, additive).

DECOMPOSITION:
- Filed as new child bead (see next): 'Extend ValidationPolicy with required_leaf_policy_oids + DnAttrRule + chain_walk enforcement.'
- PKIX-jbvb.1 / .2 / .3 (Organization / Sponsor / Individual profiles) re-blocked on the new child. Each tier's Profile::policy() populates the new fields.

This bead (the parent feature umbrella) stays open as the rollup. human label dropped — the design decision is settled and downstream work is autonomous.
